summary: Chinese ‘prepositions’ are coverbs — words that are (or were) verbs. With their noun they stand BEFORE the main verb, never after it: 我在家吃饭 ‘I eat at home’ (literally ‘I be-at home eat’). The order is fixed: subject – (time) – coverb + noun – verb – object. 在 does ‘in’ and ‘at’: 在学校, 在超市, 在银行工作. ‘To’ is the movement verb itself — 去学校 ‘go to school’ (S13) — or 到 + place + verb ‘go to … to do …’: 到超市买牛奶. 从 is ‘from’, 跟 / 和 + person + 一起 is ‘with’, 给 + person is ‘for’ (formal 为), 关于 + topic + 的 + noun is ‘about’. ‘Without’ has no word: 没有 + noun or 不 + verb. Place nouns need nothing more (在学校); ordinary nouns take a place word after them (在冰箱里, S12). There are no cases: the noun never changes.

blocks.caption: In, at, to, from, with, for, about, without — in Chinese

notes.text: Greek σε covers ‘at’ and ‘to’ (στο σπίτι, πάω στο σχολείο); Chinese splits it into 在 and 去 / 到. από is 从 for a place you leave and 离 for a distance; με is 跟 … 一起 with a person but 加 / 用 with a thing; για is 给 / 为 for a person, 关于 for a topic; χωρίς is 没有 + noun or 不 + verb.
Spanish en ~ 在 (estoy en casa), but a ‘to’ has no word: ir a la escuela ~ 去学校. con is 跟 … 一起 for people and 用 / 加 for things; para ~ 给 / 为; sin ~ 没有 / 不.
French à covers ‘at’ and ‘to’ (à la maison, je vais à l’école); Chinese splits it into 在 and 去. avec is 跟 … 一起 for people and 用 / 加 for things; pour ~ 给; sans ~ 没有 / 不.

blocks.title: Being somewhere and going somewhere are two different words
blocks.text: 在 is for being or doing something somewhere (我在学校, 我在学校吃饭); going there is a verb of movement with the place as its object (我去学校 — no word for ‘to’ at all).

blocks.title: Not at the end
blocks.text: *我吃饭在家, *我工作在银行 put the phrase after the verb — wrong in Chinese. The coverb phrase goes before the verb: 我在家吃饭, 我在银行工作.

items.title: 在 + place — where it is / happens
points: 他在医院。 He is at the hospital.
他在医院工作。 He works at the hospital.

items.title: 到 + place — where you get to
points: 我们到超市买牛奶。 We go to the supermarket to buy milk.
从我家到学校很近。 From my home to the school it is close.

blocks.title: Places need no ‘in / at’ word — things need a place word
blocks.text: 在学校, 在超市, 在银行, 在家 — these nouns are places already. A thing becomes a place with 里 / 上 after it: 在冰箱里, 在桌子上 (S12).

blocks.title: Measure words for places (S11)
blocks.text: 家 for businesses: 一家超市, 这家饭馆, 两家银行 · 所 for schools and hospitals: 一所学校, 这所大学 · 条 for streets: 一条街 · 个 for most others: 一个公园, 一个国家.

blocks.title: 跟 is ‘with’ a person only
blocks.text: 我跟朋友一起吃饭 ‘I eat with friends’ — but ‘coffee with milk’ is 加牛奶的咖啡 and ‘eat with chopsticks’ 用筷子吃饭.

blocks.title: Asking with the coverbs
blocks.text: The question word takes the noun’s place: 你在哪里工作？ 你跟谁一起吃饭？ 这是给谁的？ 这些苹果是从哪里买的？

askYourself: Where is it, or where does it happen? → 在 + place, before the verb.
Where to? → 去 + place (go), or 到 + place + verb (go there to do it).
From where? → 从 + place, before the verb. A distance (near, far)? → 离 (S12).
With whom? → 跟 / 和 + person + 一起 + verb.
With a thing (milk, chopsticks)? → not 跟: 加, 用.
For whom? → 给 + person + verb (formal 为); ‘this is for you’ = 这是给你的.
About what? → 关于 + topic + 的 + noun, or 关于… at the start.
Without? → 没有 + noun, or 不 + verb.
Is the noun a real place (school, bank, home) or a thing (fridge, table)? → a thing needs 里 / 上 after it.
Did I put the phrase at the end, after the verb? → move it before the verb.
steps: Then (time and) the coverb with its noun.
Then the verb and its object.

traps: *我吃饭在家 → 我在家吃饭.
*我去到学校 for ‘I go to school’ → 我去学校 (去 already means ‘go to’).
*我喝咖啡跟牛奶 for ‘coffee with milk’ → 我喝加牛奶的咖啡.
*一本书关于家庭 → 一本关于家庭的书 (the 关于 phrase before the noun, with 的).
*这是给你 → 这是给你的 (‘this is for you’ needs 的).
*我从家很远 for ‘I live far from home’ → distance takes 离: 我家离这里很远.
*在冰箱 for ‘in the fridge’ → 在冰箱里 (a thing needs a place word).

quiz.why: The coverb phrase 在银行 comes before the verb.
For ‘to’ the verb of movement takes the place directly; 在 is only for where you are.
给 + person + 的: ‘the one for you’.
The 关于 phrase stands before the noun, joined with 的.

quiz.q: Which word is ‘from’ for a starting point?
quiz.why: 从 = from (a place, a time); 离 is for distance, 到 for ‘to’.
Chinese has no ‘without’: 没有 + noun.
Shops and businesses are counted with 家.

notes.text: Greek prepositional phrases follow the verb (τρώω στο σπίτι, δουλεύω σε τράπεζα); Chinese coverb phrases go before it: 我在家吃饭, 我在银行工作.
Russian prepositions govern cases (в доме, в дом, из дома, с другом) and usually follow the verb; Chinese coverbs take an unchanged noun and stand before the verb: 我在家吃饭, 我跟朋友一起吃饭.
Spanish puts the phrase after the verb (como en casa, trabajo en un banco); Chinese before it: 我在家吃饭, 我在银行工作.
English puts the prepositional phrase after the verb (I eat at home, I work at a bank); Chinese puts it before: 我在家吃饭, 我在银行工作. ‘with’ is 跟 … 一起 for people but 用 / 加 for things.
French phrases follow the verb (je mange à la maison); Chinese ones precede it: 我在家吃饭.
German prepositions govern case and tell location from direction (im Haus / ins Haus); Chinese has no case — 在 is location, and a movement verb gives the direction (去学校).

Hindi postposition phrases (घर में ‘at home’, दोस्त के साथ ‘with a friend’) stand before the verb, as Chinese coverb phrases do (我在家吃饭); but Hindi puts the marker after the noun, Chinese before it (在 + 家).
Persian prepositional phrases (dar khāne, bā dust) come before the verb — the Chinese position: man dar khāne ghazā mikhoram ~ 我在家吃饭.

Marathi marks place and company after the noun (घरी ‘at home’, मित्राबरोबर ‘with a friend’) and puts them before the verb — the Chinese position, though Chinese puts its coverb before the noun: 在家, 跟朋友.
Arabic prepositions follow the verb (ākulu fī l-bayt) and put the noun in the genitive; Chinese coverbs come before the verb and the noun never changes: 我在家吃饭.
Hebrew prepositions follow the verb and often fuse with the article (ba-bayit ‘at home’); Chinese 在家 stands before the verb: 我在家吃饭.
Turkish case endings and postpositions (evde, arkadaşımla) come before the verb — the Chinese position — but after the noun; Chinese coverbs stand before the noun: 在家, 跟朋友.
Japanese particles (家で, 友達と) follow the noun and stand before the verb; Chinese coverbs precede the noun, but the phrase also goes before the verb: 在家吃饭 ~ 家で食べる.
Korean particles (집에서, 친구하고) follow the noun and stand before the verb; Chinese coverbs precede the noun, and the phrase also stands before the verb: 在家吃饭 ~ 집에서 밥을 먹어요.

Finnish uses case endings for in / from / into (talossa, talosta, taloon) and usually puts them after the verb; Chinese has no case: 在 + place before the verb, and the direction comes from the verb (去, 从 … 来).
Hungarian uses case endings (házban, házba, házból) and postpositions; Chinese has no case — 在 + place before the verb, 去 and 从 for direction.
Swahili marks place with -ni (nyumbani ‘at home’) and company with na, after the verb; Chinese puts 在家 and 跟朋友 before the verb.
Luganda puts place phrases (mu nnyumba ‘in the house’) after the verb; Chinese puts 在 + place before it.

Vietnamese also has verb-like prepositions (ở ‘be at’, cho ‘give, for’) — the same idea as 在 and 给 — but usually puts the phrase after the verb (tôi làm việc ở ngân hàng); Chinese puts it before: 我在银行工作.
Inuktitut marks place, goal and source with case endings on the noun (-mi ‘at’, -mut ‘to’, -mit ‘from’); Chinese has no endings and uses separate coverbs before the verb: 在家, 从家.

seeAlso.note: German splits σε into in / an / zu / nach and needs a case after every preposition; Chinese has no cases — 在 for ‘where’, a verb of movement for ‘where to’, and the phrase before the verb.
Wo? (dative) vs Wohin? (accusative) is a case contrast in German; Chinese says the same with two different words, 在 vs 去 / 到.
Arabic fī, ilā, min, maʿa, li- and ʿan put the noun in the genitive and follow the verb; Chinese coverbs come before the verb and change nothing.
Hebrew writes בְּ, לְ, מִ as prefixes on the noun (בַּבַּיִת ‘at home’); Chinese uses separate coverbs (在家).
